On the east side of Woodlawn, the blocks closest to the Center, the median price of a single-family home doubled between 2019 and 2025, to about 440,000 dollars.

Pull the lens back to the city's whole Jackson Park housing pilot area, and the change is starker.

In 2024, about a third of the housing stock nearby still counted as affordable.
Fifteen years before, it had been roughly two-thirds.
In September 2020, after a campaign of about five years, the City Council passed the Woodlawn Housing Preservation Ordinance.
On paper it was real protection.
It reserved 52 city-owned vacant lots for affordable housing.
It set up a loan fund, home-repair grants for longtime owners, and a right of first refusal that was supposed to give tenants a shot at buying their building before it sold out from under them.
